newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana opposes immunity for tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana opposes immunity for tobacco companies.

text.p: Louisiana's top lawyer said on Wednesday attorneys general in states suing tobacco companies were united in opposing blanket immunity from future legal action, but he did not rule out partial immunity.
"We have taken the position that there can be no blanket immunity, no complete immunity against certain actions," state Attorney General Richard Ieyoub told Reuters.

When asked if the states' legal advisers were considering partial or limited immunity for the tobacco giants, he said, "We're negotiating under rules of confidentiality and I can't get into that now."
Cigarette makers and anti-tobacco leaders have been in talks recently to reach a settlement that would resolve a multitude of anti-tobacco lawsuits in the United States.

News reports have said the tobacco industry might pay up to $300 billion over 25 years to compensate states for treating smokers with tobacco-related ills in exchange for broad protection from further legal action.
Louisiana was among the first five of 23 states to sue the tobacco companies to recoup costs incurred by taxpayers from treating indigent smokers through the Medicaid program.
On Monday, Texas Attorney General Dan Morales also said he would oppose any settlement with tobacco companies that would give them immunity from future legal action.
He said in a letter to members of the Texas Legislature the tobacco industry did not deserve immunity because it "has reneged on every promise it has ever made to the American people."

A lawsuit filed by Morales in March 1996 on behalf of the state of Texas, seeking $4 billion in damages from tobacco companies to recover Medicaid costs of smokers, is scheduled for trial Sept. 29 in federal court in Texarkana, Texas.
